w: As part of summer vacation, the Amdavad Kishore Mandal had successfully organised a cricket tournament that involved all the kishores. Members of the winning and runner-up teams had come to Swamishri for blessings. The kishores asked two interesting questions to Swamishri.

Q: Swami, what type of fielding should we do to catch your agna? A: The Amdavad Kishore Mandal organised a cricket tournament to please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Yogiji Maharaj. One can see from the above question that the motive of the tournament was to become spiritually conscious. Like Pujya Bhagatji Maharaj, who instantly observed the agna of Gunatitanand Swami, we too should do the same. One should have faith and trust in the Guru’s word and not doubt his words. One's faith should be like the agna of calling Girnar.

Q: Every time maya runs us out. What type of batting should we do so that we don’t get out? A: Gunatitanand Swami has said in his talks that when one attains true knowledge one will not get entrapped by maya. True knowledge means the knowledge of atma and Parmatma. Because we have deh bhava (body consciousness), maya runs us out. One should have a firm resolve that no matter what difficulty or pain comes, one’s atma bhava (atma conscousness) should remain steadfast and the conviction that God is the all-doer and whatever He does is for one’s good.

In the evening, the Children's Day saw various presentations and performances by the balaks and their tutors. Children performed a drama, 'Chhiye ame to chhotaji', a dance and another drama depicting the different obstacles they could face for the construction of the new mandir in Leicester. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly, emphasizing on the need of mandirs in society: "Today some people say where is the need for mandirs? But if someone were to say where is the need for colleges? Where is the need for hospitals? And are military and police required? Where is the need for courts and judges? Does one ever feel why pile stones for all this? How mad one would be if one were to speak in this manner? Similarly, one who says where is the need for mandirs is mad. Through mandirs one's mind becomes pure. Through the association of a Sadhu one finds the right path. It is not merely a place to sit and ring a bell, but through it so many services are offered to society. Children are inspired with character from a young age..."

A special Youth Day assembly was arranged for youths residing in Amdavad, Gandhinagar and Mahesana. In all, 4,500 youths had assembled. The assembly commenced with dhun, prayer and bhajans by youths. The theme of the assembly was, “Tamara Hriday Akashma Pankhi Bani Udiya Karu”. An interview was arranged with Ishwarcharan Swami and Viveksagar Swami who elaborated upon the youth training given by Yogiji Maharaj and their experiences with Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Swamishri arrived at 11.00 am. The stage backdrop had a giant heart with a bird in a flying pose. Swamishri was welcomed by youths, dressed in white, dancing to the theme song. Several youths who had been observing various satsang niyams received Swamishri’s blessings. Thereafter a wonderful dialogue took place in a skit format. Swamishri gave guidance to youth-related issues like fashion, eating out and marriage. The assembly concluded with the singing of “Re Sagapan Harivarnu Sachu” by the youths.

st.t: Grand Yuvak-Yuvti Assembly, 24 June 2006, Amdavad, India
w: On Saturday 24 June 2006, over 2,100 yuvaks and 1,700 yuvatis attended a special assembly at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Amdavad, in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.
In addition to 3,200 youths from Amdavad, youths from Gandhinagar, Mahesana, Dholka, Himmatnagar, and villages surrounding Amdavad also attended this special morning assembly.
Based on the theme 'Tamara hraday akashma pankhi bani udya karu...' the youths were inspired to strengthen their personal practice of satsang and their devotion to God and guru.

The assembly began at 9.45 am with bhajans, a speech and video show. this was followed by an inspiring question-answer session with Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami and Pujya Viveksagar Swami. Through their answers they related personal memories of Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj and how both these great gurus had inspired them on the path of spirituality.

At 11.05 am Swamishri arrived in the assembly to a rapturous ovation. The youths performed a welcome dance based on the day's theme song, 'Tamara hraday akshama...'. Thereafter, Swamishri blessed a number of youths who for many years had been sincerely practising vows of not watching TV, not eating outside food, not attending garba, observing waterless fasts on ekadashi and nom , regular satsang reading, daily singing chesta and others. Then eight youths interacted in an entertaining and enlightening discussion with Swamishri. During the discussion the youths presented the tendency of youths to be drawn away from observance of satsang vows. In particular they discussed the issues of tilak-chandlo, appropriate dress sense, eating outside food and marriage. Swamishri gave excellent guidance on each of the issues, stressing the need for all youths to apply tilak-chandlo, wear appropriate dress as directed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, not eat outside foods, and to enter into marriage as per the traditions of Hindu dharma and with the consent of their parents.

Following this absorbing and elevating discussion, the entire assembly sang the bhajan, 'Re sagapan Harivarnu sachu...' in chorus as a pledge to live by the ideals of Satsang taught by Bhagwan Swaminarayan. The atmosphere was charged with emotion and divinity.
The assembly concluded at 12.25 pm. Before they departed the youths were presented with mementoes and they pledged to sincerely live by the words of Swamishri and earn his inner blessings.

Swamishri arrived in Houston the previous day at 12.05 pm from Chicago. The Sugarland Mayor Pro Tem Dennis Parmar welcomed Swamishri at the Sugarland regional airport and presented a proclamation. The evening welcome assembly was arranged in honour of Swamishri. The assembly was held in a giant marquee in the mandir precincts. A three dimensional replica of Akshardham was the highlight of the stage backdrop. After Swamishri’s arrival BAPS teenagers and youths performed a traditional welcome dance. Then, on behalf of everyone, Tyagvallabh Swami and Viveksagar Swami garlanded Swamishri. The consul general of India in Houston Shri Shankar Gavai addressed the assembly, “I am really honoured to be here and I welcome Pramukh Swamiji. I had just sat with him for half an hour and he conveyed his simple message on humanity and spiritualism. The volunteer work exercised by the volunteers is exemplary for all.” More than 28 heads of different social and religious organizations welcomed Swamishri with bouquets. The BAPS children and teenagers performed a welcome dance. Finally, BAPS children and teenagers performed another welcome dance. Thereafter Swamishri crowned the assembly with his blessings, “We should never forget our wealth, culture and values while doing our jobs or business. You have come from India, bringing with you your dharma, culture and values. Like the way you look after your money, which you will later give to your children, look after our spiritual wealth and give it as a legacy to your children. Our culture is ancient. Bhagwan Ram and Krishna incarnated on earth. One should read the wonderful Vedas, Upanishads, Gita, Ramayan and other shastras. Daily reading of shastras will purify one’s thoughts and life. Just as you take care of your needs and use objects, similarly you must read our spiritual books, do puja and keep a mandir in the house.” More than 4,000 devotees were present. In the following days Kishore Day, Children’s Day and Youth Day were celebrated.
During the satsang assembly held in Yogi Sabhagruh on Sunday 21st Swamishri steered the decorative rath of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj and Jabreshwar Maharaj with a remote controlled console.

Today, at 4.00 pm a rath yatra was organized on a large scale on the streets of Dadar. Swamishri performed pujan and arti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, Jabreshwar Maharaj and Shri Dakshineshwar Maharaj, who were placed in two decorative palanquins. Senior sadhus carried the palanquins on the streets with the accompaniment of tunes played by a music band and bhajans sung by sadhus. Children dressed in costumes of all Indian states enthusiastically danced in traditional fashion. With male and female devotees participating, the rath yatra procession was 1 km long. The route included Matunga, King Circle, Pritam Hotel and back to the mandir in Dadar. The rath yatra concluded at 7.00 pm.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj -Mumbai Page-1, 24 June 2009
w: The Rath Yatra festival was celebrated with a grand procession for Thakorji. Initially Swamishri performed pujan and arti of Thakorji and then flagged off the procession. Thereafter sadhus and devotees carried the palanquin of Thakorji with devotion and festivity through the streets of Dadar, Mumbai.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj also blessed Rajkumar Dhoot, owner of the Videocon company and a member of the Rajya Sabha.
He said, "I have had your darshan after many days. I feel very good at your darshan."
Swamishri responded to his feeling in a different way and said, "It is God's work and God does it."
Rajkumar said, "This Akshardham is famous all over the world."
Swamishri said, "It is all God's grace."

Rajkumar said, "Jacob Zuma, President of South Africa, came here to Akshardham before becoming President, and you blessed him on the phone right here in Akshardham that he would become President, and with your blessings he became President. When he came back to India, he phoned me and said that he wanted to go to Swamiji's ashram. It is only with your blessings that he became President."
A spiritual seeker asked Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "How can the mind become focused?"
Swamishri said, "Wear a kanthi around your neck, pray, and if even a slight thought comes, keep chanting Swaminarayan... Swaminarayan.... If you fix your mind on God, it will be fixed on everything."

In the evening General Vijay Kapoor, head of the Indian armed forces, came for darshan. He had retired just two months earlier. Having served in the army for 43 years, he has won every award given in the army.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj honoured him by placing a garland on him. He sat on a chair in front.

Shri Kapoor said, "I am sorry that despite being here for four years we could not come to this Akshardham. I saw the systems and methods you people have created for the arrangements, and I was very happy to see them and felt that there is also an organisation in the country that can run itself in this way. You are the leader of this organisation. The credit goes to you."
Swamishri said, "God is the leader of all. Everything comes from him."
Shri Kapoor said, "While seeing Akshardham, I expressed a wish for your darshan. We have come to receive the blessings of a great intellectual like you."

Swamishri said, "You too serve the country well, so God is pleased. Your feeling is that unity remains in the country. Such a feeling is a virtue of God, it is given by God. You too have done good work for the country."

Shri Kapoor said, "I saw the discipline of your organisation. If such discipline could be spread throughout the country, the whole country would benefit. There are many areas in the country that are still backward. Naxalism is going on in places. In many places some trouble or other is going on, which stops the country from going forward. But if your system, which I have seen, and the way you have organised things, were spread to others, it would be very good."

After describing the work of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the divine episodes of his birth and so on, Swamishri said, "All this system has been given by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, and he has said: do devotion to God and keep your conduct and thoughts pure. And our guru always used to say, 'May God do good to all.' May he do good not only to us but to others too."

Shri Kapoor said, "It is amazing that even at this age you keep travelling outside, and what you have established is very good for all people. For everyone who comes to visit India, Akshardham is a great landmark. It is a good place to see India's glorious past. Seeing it here, our heads rise with pride. People from outside, after seeing Akshardham, express an even better opinion than of the Taj Mahal. That day when I came here, I was very happy to see the volunteers here who took me around, the security system and how every system was followed. If I have seen such arrangements and systems anywhere outside the armed forces, it is only here, and I too am proud of this. That you are running such a system is a very good thing."
Swamishri remembered Brigadier Rajsitapati, who is engaged in this seva at Akshardham.

Shri Kapoor said, "Brigadier Sitapati is a number 1 officer. It is very good that he has received your blessings. I too received your blessings and felt very good." Then he said, "Your blessings should be on the whole of India."

st.t: Sadhus meet PM Narendra Modi to convey Pramukh Swami’s blessings
w: BAPS Sadhus visited the Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi to convey His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s blessings and prayers. Swamishri had conveyed his prayers for the nation, and for the PM to lead with compassion and care for all. His blessings were conveyed to the PM on this courtesy call by Pujya Ishwarcharan Swami, Atmaswarup Swami, Brahmavihari Swami and Gnanmuni Swami.

Today, after performing the first arti of the newly installed murti of Nilkanth Varni Maharaj, Mahant Swami Maharaj took his leave. As he came out, Mangalnidhidas Swami said, "Right now there is a forecast of a severe tornado in Robbinsville. If it comes, there will be great damage."
With a gesture, Swamishri said, "It will go away." And truly, by Swamishri's blessings, the tornado disappeared into the sea.
Everyone felt as if control of the weather department were in Swamishri's hands.
While eating, Mahant Swami Maharaj, concerned about the officers from the government serving on security during his stay here, asked, "Where do these people eat?"
Anupamdas Swami said, "They eat here once, and the other time they go out and eat on their own."
When the officers were told about this, they were very pleased: "Such a great sadhu cares so much about us!"
Whether a devoted satsangi or a security officer, Swamishri cares for everyone.
After Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, he sat for about a minute and a half with his eyes closed. The attendant asked, "What did you do?"
Swamishri said, "I said the shloka."
As soon as Swamishri sat on his seat, everyone had started saying the shloka. With the thal being arranged, Swamishri had not been able to join fully in singing the shloka. So
he said the shloka again, calmly and with concentration.
One who never forgets Bhagwan even for a moment surely behaves like this only to inspire us!
